items.fact: PC Gamer's mission list says the campaign has five chapters and 91 story missions, but Push Square and Insider Gaming count 93, so the total varies by source and by whether optional missions are included.
The chapters are Just Like Paradise (Leonida Keys), Paradise Lost (Port Gellhorn), Tits, Ass, Drug Money (Vice City), Vice City, Baby, and Top of the World, Ma.
Main missions per chapter are 22, 11 plus 3 optional, 26 plus 1 optional, 25, and 7, and the final mission is titled The End of the Road.
You play as Jason and Lucia. Chapter 1 is Jason alone as a drug runner in the Keys, and Lucia joins after her release from prison.

Chapter 2 ends with the mission Checking Out, when Jason and Lucia leave Port Gellhorn for Vice City, and several optional missions (Thrillbillies, Twist Wrist, Smash, Grab, and others) are worth doing before then.
Leonida has six main regions: Vice City, the Leonida Keys, Grassrivers, Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia and Mount Kalaga National Park. Rockstar says the map is about twice the size of GTA 5's.
There are 18 collectible card sets. Cards can be sold at pawn shops, and you can view your collection through a wooden box in your apartment.
Dexerto has pinned 103 collectible cards on its map so far, and the Nine1Nine set alone has 36 cards, which sell for $9,600 in total.
The Chapter 2 motel has several collectibles you should grab before leaving, including figures such as Bryson Powers and Vicki and magazines such as Wizard Wang.
After the Island Dreams mission, Kenton in Key Lento unlocks underwater treasure dives, and each haul sells for around $2,600.
There are 40 unique race locations. Racing costs an entry fee plus a vehicle rental fee, but winning pays a profit.
Large bank vault robberies pay up to $200,000, but they unlock near the end of Chapter 4, and the robbery instantly gives you a 4-star wanted level.
Moses (Chapter 2) buys untracked stolen cars for roughly $1,000 to $5,000 each, and Randy's wish list of 18 high-end sports cars pays $30,000 or more per car from partway through Chapter 3.
Jewelry store robberies, unlocked in Chapter 3, pay roughly $10,000 to $25,000 each.
Banks and loan stores have dye packs that explode if you walk away with them, so wait for the dye pack jammer in Chapter 3 before robbing them.
Buses and trains give fast travel across Leonida's network, but they run on a schedule. Medium- or high-security robberies are much easier if you bring Jason or Lucia along.
Check stolen cars for trackers with the WAiNK app before delivering them, because tracked vehicles can't be sold.

Ultimate Edition vehicles are found in-game: a Dinka Enduro motorcycle and Crest Kayak at Jason's house in Key Lento, a '67 Dominator Buggy in your Paradise garage from Chapter 2, and a Shitzu Squalo from Chapter 4.

Update 01.002.002 (Nov 23) fixes crashes, autosave failures, static weather, phone calls that didn't trigger, and wanted levels that couldn't be cleared. It also fixes the gym deadlift bar and partners not handing over bags to sell to fences.
The patch is about 603.7 MB on PS5 and 1.6 GB on Xbox Series X|S, and the base game is a 211 GB download.
Players reported autosaves vanishing and losing hours of progress before the patch, so saving manually is still a sensible habit.
The patch notes don't mention the glitch that forces first-person view or the Xbox glitch that unlocks 60fps, and the money withdrawal system for the stash and ATMs is also still clunky.
